content:
rajesh: quick heads-up — ran a small apples-to-apples mini harness to repro the p99 regression we saw after the batching heuristic change.

rajesh: setup: replay trace (workload-x86-2025), kvcache=on, concurrent_clients=24, small_batch_threshold=8 -> kernel selection was 'small-matmul' for many heads.

maria: can you paste the harness command + a short profile?

rajesh: here you go:
```
./tools/replay --trace traces/workload-x86-2025.pb --kvcache=enabled --concurrency=24 --batch-heuristic=small_batch_threshold=8 --kernel-policy=auto --out=result.json
```

rajesh: lightweight perf sample from the run (aggregated):
```
perf-summary: total_tokens=12.3M p50=32ms p95=180ms p99=420ms
kernel_select: 10.8%
attn.matmul: 47.2%
kv_cache_lock_wait: 9.6%
small-matmul-kernel: 21.0%
large-matmul-kernel: 11.4%
```

perf-bot: [auto] flame-summary attached: kernel_select hotspots flagged (rule=kernel-mismatch).

sophia: that kv_cache_lock_wait number stands out. small-matmul produces shorter per-call matmuls but increases call rate; with concurrent eviction/warmup we probably have more KV lock contention.

maria: hypothesis: the batching heuristic pushed many requests into smaller kernels and that increased kernel-switch overhead + more frequent KV cache checks.

sophia: quick experiment suggestion — force kernel_policy=prefer_large for the same harness and measure p99. also try increasing small_batch_threshold to 12 to see trend.

rajesh: will run both. can someone confirm the exact two configs to run so results are apples-to-apples? want identical seeds and replay timeline.

maria: run A = baseline: small_batch_threshold=16, kernel_policy=auto.
run B = test: small_batch_threshold=8, kernel_policy=prefer_large (only kernel_policy changed vs auto). keep concurrency/hot prefixes same. tag outputs `mini-kernel-switch-1765432100`.

sophia: example config snippet to inject:
```
{"batching": {"small_batch_threshold": 8}, "kernel": {"policy": "prefer_large"}, "replay": {"seed": 42}}
```

rajesh: kicked off run B now (job id replay-1765432100-b). will paste numbers when done.

rajesh: results B vs A (after paired runs):
- p99: A=420ms, B=370ms (~12% reduction)
- p95: A=180ms, B=165ms
- throughput (tokens/s): A=5200, B=5080 (~2.3% drop)
- kv_cache_lock_wait: A=9.6%, B=6.1%

maria: nice — lower tail and less KV lock wait, small throughput tradeoff looks acceptable for latency-sensitive routes.

sophia: sounds like kernel selection was the vector. follow-ups: 1) measure with higher concurrency (48) to stress eviction, 2) check correctness under concurrent prefix eviction (sanity tests), 3) instrument finer-grained KV lock timing.

rajesh: i'll open a perf PR with the paired-run logs and config diffs. also will run the 48 client test and post results in this thread.

maria: please add a short note linking the replay job ids and include the perf-summary snippets. put `perf:kv-kernel-switch` label on the PR. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: [auto] replay-1765432100-b completed, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/mini-kernel-switch/1765432100-b/

rajesh: thanks. scheduling a canary experiment Monday to try prefer_large on latency-critical route (will coordinate with oncall).

sophia: if canary shows stable tail improvement, we should consider making kernel_policy heuristics aware of KV-contention signals (kv_lock_wait metric) and prefer_large when above threshold.

maria: agreed. good first repro + mitigation path.

rajesh: thanks all, closing loop here once 48-client run is in.
